summary: David E. Riggs is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of California, Los Angeles. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and the University of Hawaiʻi, and held research posts at Nichibunken and Oberlin College.

David F. Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. An associate professor at the University of Virginia (attested 2000–2008), he studied under David M. Knipe, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and others.

David Faure is a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Hong Kong and earned a sociology Ph.D. from Princeton. He taught at Indiana University, lectured at St Antony's College (1990–2006), and became a director at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

David Fiordalis works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. attested 2008) under Luis Oscar Gómez, and became associate professor and department chair at Linfield University.

David Friedman (1903–1984) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS and as a professor at the University of London from circa 1950 to 1970.
David Gonsalez is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at UW-Madison and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. c. 1988). He taught at the University of Chicago and the University of Virginia before joining the University of California, Santa Barbara in 1996.

David J. Kalupahana (1936–2014) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his Ph.D. from SOAS/University of London under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman. He taught at the University of Ceylon before chairing the philosophy department at the University of Hawaiʻi.

David Jones is a philosophy and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi. In 2007, he was attested as professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt (1937–2006) was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell (Ph.D. c. 1966). After lecturing at SOAS and Michigan, he served as history department chair at Cornell University (1969–2002) and Association for Asian Studies president (1993).
David Kerman Tomlinson is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019). He also held a post at Smith College.

David Kopf (1930–2023) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1960 to 1964 and held a faculty post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1997.

David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and was affiliated with the University of Cambridge as attested in 2001.

David L. Haberman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Colorado (1970–1974). He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1987–1993) and Indiana University (~1993).

David L. McMahan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. After teaching at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, he served at Franklin & Marshall College as assistant professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2013).

David Llewellyn Snellgrove (1920–2016) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Cambridge under D. R. Shackleton Bailey and Harold Walter Bailey, among others. He was a professor at SOAS, University of London (1950–1982) and founded the Institute of Tibetan Studies, Tring.

David Ludden is an Indologist and historian educated at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at the University of Virginia, was assistant professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and became professor of political economy and globalization at NYU in 2007.

David M. DiValerio is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer. He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (attested 2015).

David M. Knipe is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as professor (attested 1975, 1998–2001) and as Professor of South Asian Studies and Chair of Religious Studies (attested 1989).
David Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, serving as its director as attested in 2004 and remaining affiliated as attested in 2013.
